text:
vikram: thinking out loud — can we move the priority/score computation into the OTEL exporter instead of the collector? reduces backend churn and lets exporters tag spans for downstream samplers

ella: interesting. exporter has request context (route, model_id) but not always quota/tenant-tier info. how would it get that?

maria: we could embed a small tenant-profile cache in the exporter binary and sync from config service every 30s. lightweight, mostly read-only.

vikram: exactly. exporter computes: priority = base(route_weight) * tenant_multiplier - recent_error_penalty. then it attaches span.attr "ri.priority" and lets tail-sampler use it.

jordan: downside: sync lag means wrong multiplier for a short window. also increases exporter complexity and deploy surface.

ella: from a telemetry POV the big win is we can do deterministic export-time sampling keys -> stable head sampling, and still mark tail candidates. keeps collector simpler.

maria: prototype config snippet i sketched:
```
exporter:
  tenant_profile_sync: { endpoint: "https://config.internal", poll_secs: 30 }
  priority_rules:
    - match: { route: "/api/generate" }
      base: 1.2
    - match: { route: "/embeddings" }
      base: 0.7
```

vikram: also thinking about quotas: if a tenant is near quota, exporter should lower priority to avoid saving extra traces. cache needs quota signal. can we stream quota deltas via the sync endpoint?

jordan: we already emit tenant quota metrics to the internal metrics pipeline but not to the exporters. streaming deltas is doable but adds a new channel.

ella: UX question: if exporters mark spans with ri.priority, the Console sampling UI should expose that field and let infra create rules based on it. rollouts need safe defaults so customers don't accidentally drop everything.

maria: agreed. Default rule: keep all error spans + spans with ri.priority > 0.8, sample rest probabilistically. fallback to collector-level head/tail if attribute missing.

sre-bot: deploy check: exporter changes require canary in us-west-2, 5% traffic, telemetry alerting on drop-in retention.

vikram: canary plan looks good. question: do we add a deterministic sampling key (hash(route, tenant_id, req_id)) at exporter so head sampling stays stable across retries?

jordan: yes please — deterministic key avoids flapping between head/tail. key = sha256(tenant_id + route + first_trace_id) mod 10000 -> bucket.

ella: one more: retention. when we mark spans as tail-candidate, downstream should store full KV cache for that trace; otherwise tail sampling loses context. storage cost spike risk during rollout. need retention budget alerts.

maria: i'll add an alert: if tail-candidate writes per-minute > 2x baseline -> paging. also add a per-tenant retention cap in Console.

vikram: next steps: maria to build exporter prototype + config sync, jordan to spec deterministic key, ella to add Console field + default rules, i'll own canary + alerts. I'll open a short RFC now. @deploy-bot FYI canary when ready? :eyes:

deploy-bot: noted. will auto-create canary job when PR hits main and tag will be required :white_check_mark:

jordan: fwiw, simple perf numbers from my local run: exporter extra CPU ~3-5% and memory +30MB for cache of 10k tenant entries. pretty reasonable.

ella: sounds promising. also add a privacy note: tenant-profile sync only contains non-sensitive flags (tier, quota-usage-agg, sampling_overrides) — no PII.

maria: will include schema in RFC + example dashboards for retention/priority distribution.

vikram: thanks team. let's keep the thread for RFC comments, ping me if you want to pair on the prototype.
